questions.name: Pedestrian Safety and Work Platforms
questions.objective: 6.1 Identify pedestrian hazards and separation practices around forklifts
questions.text: Why are forklifts around pedestrians a serious concern?

answers.text: Pedestrians can be struck, crushed, or pinned by moving forklifts or loads
Pedestrians always have the same visibility as forklift operators
Forklifts cannot injure pedestrians at low speed
Pedestrian hazards disappear when the forklift is unloaded

explanations.a: The workbook notes that many forklift-related incidents involve pedestrians, so separation and awareness are critical. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Pedestrians and operators can both have blind spots.
explanations.c: Low-speed forklifts can still crush or strike pedestrians.
explanations.d: Unloaded forklifts still create struck-by and crush hazards.

questions.name: Pedestrian Safety and Work Platforms
questions.objective: 6.1 Identify pedestrian hazards and separation practices around forklifts
questions.text: What is a best practice for protecting pedestrians from forklift traffic?

answers.text: Rely only on pedestrians hearing the forklift
Establish clear, separate pathways for pedestrians and forklifts
Allow shortcuts through loading areas during busy periods
Let pedestrians choose any aisle when forklifts are operating

explanations.a: Noise, distractions, and blind spots can prevent timely warning.
explanations.b: Separate pathways reduce the chance that pedestrians enter forklift travel routes. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Shortcuts through active forklift areas increase exposure.
explanations.d: Uncontrolled pedestrian routes increase struck-by exposure.

questions.name: Pedestrian Safety and Work Platforms
questions.objective: 6.1 Identify pedestrian hazards and separation practices around forklifts
questions.text: During pedestrian safety training for forklift operations, where should pedestrian and forklift conflicts receive special attention?

answers.text: Solely after a pedestrian has already been struck
Solely in unused storage rooms
Near time clocks, break rooms, cafeterias, main exits, intersections, and restricted areas
Solely outside the building

explanations.a: Controls should prevent incidents before they occur.
explanations.b: Pedestrian exposure is most critical where people and forklifts interact.
explanations.c: The workbook highlights high-foot-traffic areas and restricted areas as places where forklift use should be controlled. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Pedestrian hazards occur both indoors and outdoors.

questions.name: Pedestrian Safety and Work Platforms
questions.objective: 6.1 Identify pedestrian hazards and separation practices around forklifts
questions.text: What control can help isolate workstations from aisles traveled by forklifts?

answers.text: Painted lines alone in every high-risk area
Verbal warnings without route control
A rule requiring workers to jump out of the way
Physical barriers where practical

explanations.a: Lines can help, but physical barriers may be stronger where practical.
explanations.b: Warnings alone do not separate workers from moving forklifts.
explanations.c: Workers should not rely on last-second avoidance.
explanations.d: The workbook recommends physical barriers where practical to isolate workstations from forklift aisles. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Pedestrian Safety and Work Platforms
questions.objective: 6.2 Recognize traffic controls, blind spots, intersections, and restricted areas
questions.keyword: traffic controls blind spots and restricted areas
questions.text: Why should restricted areas be clearly identified?

answers.text: So forklifts can ignore speed controls inside them
So warning signs replace all training
So workers can use restricted areas as shortcuts
So pedestrians and operators understand where forklift movement or entry is limited

explanations.a: Restricted areas still require safe operation.
explanations.b: Signs support but do not replace training and communication.
explanations.c: Restricted areas should not become pedestrian shortcuts.
explanations.d: Clear identification helps prevent unauthorized entry into hazardous forklift operating zones. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Pedestrian Safety and Work Platforms
questions.objective: 6.2 Recognize traffic controls, blind spots, intersections, and restricted areas
questions.keyword: traffic controls blind spots and restricted areas
questions.text: An operator is working in a shared area with pedestrians. What should be done at blind spots and intersections?

answers.text: Minimize blind spots, highlight intersections, and use caution before entering
Ignore intersections when the forklift has no load
Accelerate through the intersection to reduce time exposed
Assume mirrors eliminate every blind spot

explanations.a: The workbook recommends minimizing blind spots and highlighting intersections and restricted areas. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Unloaded forklifts still can strike pedestrians or vehicles.
explanations.c: Speeding through blind areas increases collision risk.
explanations.d: Mirrors may help but do not remove every visibility limitation.

questions.name: Pedestrian Safety and Work Platforms
questions.objective: 6.2 Recognize traffic controls, blind spots, intersections, and restricted areas

questions.text: Which area should have restricted forklift use during peak pedestrian flow?

answers.text: Remote aisles with no pedestrian access
Near time clocks, break rooms, cafeterias, and main exits
Areas where forklifts are stored with power off
Any area just because the floor is painted

explanations.a: The concern is highest where pedestrian flow is concentrated.

explanations.c: Stored inactive equipment creates a different hazard profile.
explanations.d: Answer boundary: restrictions should be based on actual traffic and hazard exposure.

questions.objective: 6.2 Recognize traffic controls, blind spots, intersections, and restricted areas

questions.text: What is an effective traffic-control approach in forklift areas?

answers.text: Allowing forklifts and pedestrians to merge without control
Removing route markings because operators know the site
Defined travel lanes, signs, signals, barriers, and controlled access
Changing traffic rules without telling workers

explanations.c: Traffic controls help organize forklift movement and pedestrian access to prevent collisions. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Unexpected rules can create confusion.

questions.name: Pedestrian Safety and Work Platforms
questions.objective: 6.3 Identify communication, warning, horn, high-visibility, and proximity alert practices
questions.text: When can proximity detection lights be helpful?

answers.text: Solely when forklifts are parked and shut off
As permission to travel faster near pedestrians
Where ambient noise is high or pedestrians need visual warning that a forklift is moving or changing direction
As a replacement for operator attention

explanations.a: Proximity warnings are most relevant during movement or direction changes.
explanations.b: Warning devices do not justify higher speed.
explanations.c: The workbook recommends proximity detection lights where noise levels are high and visual alerts can warn pedestrians. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Operators must still look, communicate, and control the forklift.

questions.name: Pedestrian Safety and Work Platforms
questions.objective: 6.3 Identify communication, warning, horn, high-visibility, and proximity alert practices
questions.text: Which statement best addresses communication warnings and visibility? Which communication practice best supports pedestrian safety?

answers.text: Assume pedestrians know the operator's intended path
Wave pedestrians through a blind travel path without checking traffic
Use conflicting signals from different spotters
Use clear signals, eye contact when possible, and stop if pedestrian movement is uncertain

explanations.a: Pedestrians may not know the forklift route or load swing.
explanations.b: Answer boundary: pedestrians should not be directed into uncontrolled hazards.
explanations.c: Conflicting signals can create dangerous misunderstandings.
explanations.d: Clear communication and stopping when uncertain reduce struck-by and crush hazards. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Pedestrian Safety and Work Platforms
questions.objective: 6.3 Identify communication, warning, horn, high-visibility, and proximity alert practices
questions.text: When should a forklift operator sound the horn?

answers.text: When approaching corners, blind areas, or other locations where warning is needed
Continuously in all areas with no regard to conditions
Never when pedestrians are nearby
Solely after hitting an object

explanations.a: The workbook instructs operators to sound the horn when approaching corners and blind areas. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Horn use should warn at appropriate points and not replace controlled operation.
explanations.c: Pedestrians often need warning when visibility is limited.
explanations.d: Warnings should occur before exposure.

To help operators see pedestrians, especially outside designated walkways
To replace pedestrian walkways
To protect workers from falling loads

explanations.c: High-visibility clothing helps but does not replace separation.
explanations.d: High-visibility apparel improves visibility, not falling-object protection.

questions.name: Pedestrian Safety and Work Platforms
questions.objective: 6.4 Apply safe practices for lifting people on forklift work platforms
questions.text: How must a forklift work platform be secured?

answers.text: Balanced loosely on the fork tips
Firmly secured to the carriage or forks to prevent displacement
Held in place by the worker's weight
Secured only with verbal instructions

explanations.a: Loose placement can allow the platform to shift or fall.
explanations.b: The workbook requires the platform to be firmly secured to prevent displacement. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Worker weight is not a secure attachment method.
explanations.d: Instructions do not physically prevent displacement.

questions.name: Pedestrian Safety and Work Platforms
questions.objective: 6.4 Apply safe practices for lifting people on forklift work platforms
questions.text: During pedestrian safety training for forklift operations, where must the forklift operator be while workers are on the elevated platform?

answers.text: Standing on the platform with the workers
Away from the controls while the platform is raised
With the forklift, in the normal operating position when raising and lowering the platform
In the break room until workers call down

explanations.a: The operator must operate from the normal operating position.
explanations.b: The operator needs to remain with the forklift and control the movement.
explanations.c: The workbook says the operator must stay with the forklift and be in the normal operating position when raising and lowering the platform. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: The operator must stay with the forklift.

questions.name: Pedestrian Safety and Work Platforms
questions.objective: 6.4 Apply safe practices for lifting people on forklift work platforms
questions.text: What is the travel restriction when workers are on an elevated work platform?

answers.text: Move with the platform elevated high whenever the route is clear
Drive normally across the facility if workers hold the rails
Travel quickly so workers spend less time elevated
The forklift must not travel point to point with the platform elevated above 4 feet, except very slow inching when necessary

explanations.a: Elevated point-to-point travel is restricted even when the route appears clear.
explanations.b: Holding rails does not make elevated travel safe.
explanations.c: Speed increases fall and collision risk.
explanations.d: The workbook limits travel with workers elevated above 4 feet and allows only very slow inching when necessary. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: Pedestrian Safety and Work Platforms
questions.objective: 6.4 Apply safe practices for lifting people on forklift work platforms

explanations.b: A loose rope is not equivalent platform fall protection.
explanations.c: A pallet is not an approved work platform.
explanations.d: A sign does not protect workers from falling from the platform.

questions.name: Pedestrian Safety and Work Platforms
questions.objective: 6.5 Recognize operator and pedestrian coordination during shared-area forklift operations
questions.text: During training, an operator is working in a shared area with pedestrians. What should an operator do before backing a forklift?

answers.text: Check behind and on both sides for pedestrians or other traffic
Rely on pedestrians to move out of the way
Raise the load to make backing easier
Back immediately if the horn works

explanations.a: The workbook instructs operators to check behind and on both sides before backing. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Operators must verify the path is clear.
explanations.c: Raised loads can reduce stability and visibility.
explanations.d: A horn does not replace checking the area.

questions.name: Pedestrian Safety and Work Platforms
questions.objective: 6.5 Recognize operator and pedestrian coordination during shared-area forklift operations
questions.text: Which practice helps pedestrians working near forklift routes?

answers.text: Stand beside a fixed object when a forklift approaches
Stay in designated walkways and avoid entering forklift operating zones without communication
Walk behind forklifts because operators always see rear areas
Cut through loading areas during peak traffic

explanations.a: A pedestrian can be pinned between the forklift and fixed object.
explanations.b: Using designated walkways and communicating before entering forklift zones reduces exposure. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Operators can have rear blind spots, especially while handling loads.
explanations.d: Answer boundary: cutting through active loading areas increases struck-by risk.

questions.name: Pedestrian Safety and Work Platforms
questions.objective: 6.5 Recognize operator and pedestrian coordination during shared-area forklift operations
questions.text: What should an operator do when a pedestrian is next to a fixed object?

answers.text: Drive closer so the pedestrian can hear instructions
Use the load to nudge the pedestrian's attention
Avoid driving up to the pedestrian and stop until the hazard is controlled
Assume the pedestrian can step aside quickly

explanations.a: Driving close can crush the pedestrian against the fixed object.
explanations.b: Loads must never be used to push or signal people.
explanations.c: The workbook states operators should never drive up to someone standing next to a fixed object. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Last-second movement is not a safe control.

questions.name: Pedestrian Safety and Work Platforms
questions.objective: 6.5 Recognize operator and pedestrian coordination during shared-area forklift operations
questions.text: How should operators and pedestrians handle uncertainty about right-of-way?

answers.text: The forklift should always continue because it is powered equipment
The pedestrian should run across quickly
Both should proceed slowly and adjust at the last moment
Stop, communicate, and proceed only when movement is clear and controlled

explanations.a: Powered equipment must yield or stop when needed to prevent injury.
explanations.b: Running across forklift paths increases risk.
explanations.c: Shared guessing can cause collisions.
explanations.d: When movement is uncertain, stopping and communicating is safer than guessing. This is the correct answer.
